process_step_1_description: One hundred buyers with an age, profession, income, family composition, and attitude toward new products. Everything is written in plain words and passed to the model as a role.
process_step_2_description: The same product for everyone. Only the price changes — first raised, then discounted. That is how we compare scenarios against each other.
process_step_3_description: Not a number but a remark — like in a real interview. This matters: if you ask the model to name a score right away, it answers reluctantly and monotonously.
process_step_4_description: Five reference phrases — from “definitely won't buy” to “definitely will buy.” The program measures which one the answer resembles, by meaning rather than by word matches.

Why the system balances itself

1

Demand → orders

EMA of actual sales keeps order volume in step with the market

2

Lead time → reorder point

EMA of actual delivery delay adjusts the reorder level

3

Stock → plant plan

warehouse coverage in days drives production 55–170 %

A living, endless simulation of Aitas chilled chicken distribution: plant → warehouses → stores on the map.

​

Each step is one day. Orders are managed by a reorder point with two EMAs (store demand and actual lead time); warehouses release the oldest batches under FEFO — only those that will survive the journey and sell through in time, plus a rescue pass for stranded stock. 

​

Trips are assembled into greedy chains of up to five stores and 1500 kg, and production is throttled by warehouse coverage.

​

Every step is written to an event log and replayed on the map. An LLM analyzes it for weaknesses and oversees the process with recommendations.

How the assistant works — a brief overview for management

The assistant helps executives prepare decisions and learns from them. Four steps are described:

1. Question — the executive asks in their own words ("rising raw material prices — how do we protect margin?")

2. Context — the assistant finds similar decisions in the company's journal and the metrics linked to them (prices, production, consumption)

3. Decision — the executive records the decision following the standard: context, alternatives considered, expected outcome

4. Fact — the actual result is entered at the checkpoint, and the system itself calculates the deviation between "expected vs actual"

​

The data is still open industry data (stat.gov.kz, FAOSTAT, World Bank) plus a demo decision journal. Once the real journal data is connected, the assistant will give increasingly accurate recommendations — the more decisions are recorded, the smarter the answers

LLM talks to LLM

No human writes the prompt — agents negotiate with one another

Synthetic data

Head Buyer

Retail chain buyer

"Requesting a 9% discount on chilled chicken. Volumes are growing, and so is our shelf share"

Supplier Agent

AITAS supplier

"Ready to concede 7%. Keeps our margin and shelf share intact"

discount request

supplier response

Buyer and supplier negotiations

The chain agent requests discounts, suppliers respond with concessions. The agreements feed into the formulas.

Respondents vs Judge

One AI answers as the customer, another independently evaluates the response. Cross-checking.

Event → calculation → interpretation

One AI turns text into parameters, the core computes the numbers, another AI explains the result.

Watch video

"Chicken market scenario simulator: an event is described in text, and the engine recalculates margin, revenue, sales, and write-offs for every location on the map; interpretation is prepared by a local LLM. 

​

Three loops of dialogue between agents: monthly negotiations between the chain buyer and supplier agents — concessions turn into price multipliers and shift shelf shares; synthetic household surveys, where respondents' answers are independently checked by a strict judge; and the "event → calculation → interpretation" chain. 

​

The numbers belong solely to the deterministic formula core; every step is logged and reproducible without a single LLM call.

Structured channels  ·  Formulas own the numbers  ·  Every step is logged

inf_market_supply_subtitle: Smart distribution of chilled chicken by time in transit and selling speed: factory → warehouse → stores/supermarkets/etc.
inf_market_supply_shelf_title: Dispatch targeted at batch shelf life
inf_market_supply_shelf_p1: A batch leaves the warehouse only if it arrives and sells before the end of its shelf life. This way meat never rots on shelves or in warehouses.
inf_market_supply_buffer_note: untouched buffer until end of shelf life
inf_market_supply_rule: we dispatch if: transit + sale + 0.25 d ≤ 7 days
inf_market_supply_fefo: FEFO: the oldest batch leaves first — but only the one that passes the test. If an order is not closed, a rescue pass sends out an old batch that would at least survive the journey: stock never stagnates.
inf_market_supply_step1_text: EMA of actual sales keeps order volume behind the market
inf_market_supply_step2_text: EMA of real delivery delay adjusts the top-up level
inf_market_supply_step3_text: warehouse coverage in days throttles production 55–170 %
inf_market_scenario_label: Scenario explanation from the source presentation
inf_market_supply_scenario_p1: A live endless simulation of chilled Aitas chicken distribution: factory → warehouses → stores on the map.
inf_market_supply_scenario_p2: A step is one day. Orders are driven by a reorder point with two EMAs (store demand and actual lead time); warehouses give out the oldest batches FEFO-style — only those that survive the road and sell in time — plus a rescue pass for stuck stock.
inf_market_supply_scenario_p3: Trips are assembled greedily in chains of up to five stores and 1500 kg; production is throttled by warehouse coverage.
inf_market_supply_scenario_p4: Every step is written to an event log and replayed on the map. An LLM analyses weaknesses and monitors the process from a recommendations perspective.

inf_coord_llm_subtitle: No human writes the prompt — agents negotiate with one another
inf_coord_llm_buyer_quote: "Requesting a 9% discount on chilled chicken. Volumes are growing, and so is our shelf share"
inf_coord_llm_supplier_quote: "Ready to concede 7%. Keeps our margin and shelf share intact"
inf_coord_llm_c1_desc: The chain agent requests discounts, suppliers respond with concessions. The agreements feed into the formulas.
inf_coord_llm_c2_desc: One AI answers as the customer, another independently evaluates the response. Cross-checking.
inf_coord_llm_c3_desc: One AI turns text into parameters, the core computes the numbers, another AI explains the result.
inf_coord_llm_n1: "Chicken market scenario simulator: an event is described in text, and the engine recalculates margin, revenue, sales, and write-offs for every location on the map; interpretation is prepared by a local LLM.
inf_coord_llm_n2: Three loops of dialogue between agents: monthly negotiations between the chain buyer and supplier agents — concessions turn into price multipliers and shift shelf shares; synthetic household surveys, where respondents' answers are independently checked by a strict judge; and the "event → calculation → interpretation" chain.
inf_coord_llm_n3: The numbers belong solely to the deterministic formula core; every step is logged and reproducible without a single LLM call.
inf_coord_llm_footer: Structured channels · Formulas own the numbers · Every step is logged

inf_coord_adv_cycle_title: How the assistant works — a brief overview for management
inf_coord_adv_cycle_intro: The assistant helps executives prepare decisions and learns from them. Four steps are described:
inf_coord_adv_step1_desc: the executive asks in their own words ("rising raw material prices — how do we protect margin?")
inf_coord_adv_step2_desc: the assistant finds similar decisions in the company's journal and the metrics linked to them (prices, production, consumption)
inf_coord_adv_step3_desc: the executive records the decision following the standard: context, alternatives considered, expected outcome
inf_coord_adv_step4_desc: the actual result is entered at the checkpoint, and the system itself calculates the deviation between "expected vs actual"
inf_coord_adv_data_note: The data is still open industry data (stat.gov.kz, FAOSTAT, World Bank) plus a demo decision journal. Once the real journal data is connected, the assistant will give increasingly accurate recommendations — the more decisions are recorded, the smarter the answers.
